Andrew Chen: ok folks — planning thread for the runtime perf initiative we promised to Q3 customers. goal is to nail launch criteria + scope for kernels, quant, and KV cache work.
Maria Gomez: high-level ask from sales: enterprise customer wants p99 < 120ms on 8k context for chat workload, and 30% token-cost reduction. can we realistically hit both? :thinking_face:
Kevin Li: short answer: not at the same time for all models. kernels + kernel scheduling gives latency win; quantization yields cost win but risks quality for some models. KV cache helps both but depends on hit rate.
Tanvi Rao: propose we split into 3 deliverables: 1) kernels & scheduling optimizations (GPU path), 2) quantization profiles + validation harness, 3) KV-prefetch & eviction policies. prioritize order: 1 -> 3 -> 2 unless customer requires aggressive cost first.
Sam (product): sales says the customer will only sign if p99 target is met by launch. they care more about latency than cost. so we should prioritize latency-first for that contract.
Andrew Chen: ok that clarifies. let's define launch criteria so eng and ML know when to cut scope. suggested: p50 down 20% and p99 down 15% vs baseline for the target models; regression on eval suite <= 0.5% for critical prompts; end-to-end cost per 1k tokens <= current +10% (we accept slight cost increase).
Maria Gomez: +1 on concrete thresholds. add rollout constraints: canary to 5% traffic for 48h with automatic rollback on error rate or quality regression.
Kevin Li: implementation note: kernel work includes: fused Attention kernels, attention-only kernels for short sequences, and smarter batch packing. I estimate 6 sprints for prototype, 2 sprints for hardening. KV changes: prefix caching + probabilistic eviction, plus a Redis-based remote cache for Dedicated.
Tanvi Rao: quantization plan: produce 3 profiles per model (fp16, int8-symmetric, int8-per-channel) and run per-profile evals. we'll gate production rollout on quality metrics. this will be parallelizable but needs ML infra support.
Andrew Chen: dependencies: kernel engineers (kevin), compiler work (Tanvi), infra for canary and remote cache (eng-infra). need E2E perf harness and synthetic workloads from product.
Sam (product): I can get customer traces. please define the data share / NDA needed. they prefer not to send raw prompts; they can send token frequency and latency traces.
Maria Gomez: decision needed: do we include model fallback (lower-precision variant) in initial rollout? fallback helps availability but complicates SLOs and cost tracking.
Kevin Li: fallback is useful. proposed policy: route by priority: primary model -> quantized variant (same arch) -> smaller model only on severe load. fallback only for Dedicated/Hosted with explicit config.
Tanvi Rao: testing guardrails: for any quantized model we run the regression harness of ~2k labeled prompts and require BLEU/embedding-sim delta < 0.5% and hallucination rate measured by evals not increase > 1%.
Andrew Chen: launch criteria summary (draft):
```
- Latency: p50 <= baseline * 0.8 AND p99 <= baseline * 0.85 for target models
- Quality: eval regression <= 0.5% across core prompt sets
- Reliability: canary 0 critical errors for 48h at 5% traffic
- Cost: no >10% cost increase, prefer cost reduction
- Rollout: instant rollback on canary trigger; staged A/B for 2 weeks
```
Maria Gomez: action items and owners:
- Kernels prototype -> Kevin (6w)
- KV cache design + infra -> Andrew + eng-infra (4w)
- Quant profiles + eval harness -> Tanvi + ML infra (6w)
- Customer trace ingestion NDA -> Sam (1w)
- Canary + metrics dashboard -> Maria (2w)
Kevin Li: one more tradeoff: aggressive batching increases throughput but hurts p99 for single-request workloads. need config knobs to bias for latency vs throughput per route.
Tanvi Rao: agree — include route-level policy with priorities: latency-sensitive routes get smaller batch sizes, throughput routes use larger batching windows. we'll add this to rollout doc.
Sam (product): can we commit to a soft target date for initial canary? looks like earliest realistic is 10 weeks from now. customer wants Q3 delivery window.
Andrew Chen: tentative milestone plan: 10w prototype + 2w internal canary + 2w customer canary = 14w. call it Q3-target but flexible.
Maria Gomez: risks to highlight for execs: 1) quality regression from quantization 2) infra capacity hits from canary 3) longer kernel tuning cycle on new ops. mitigation: gated rollouts, synthetic traffic, parallelize quant validation.
Kevin Li: open question: do we include support for CPU-serving quantized paths at launch or defer to post-launch? CPU quant helps Private/on-prem customers.
Tanvi Rao: recommend defer for MVP — faster to ship GPU path then add CPU quant in Q4.
Andrew Chen: sounds reasonable. final ask: everyone add a 3-line plan + blocker list in this thread by EOD. I'll consolidate into PRD and share with execs.
runtime-bot: NOTE: new perf-ticket created RT-4821 for kernels prototype (assignee: Kevin Li).
Sam (product): thanks — I will follow up on NDA and customer expectations.
Maria Gomez: thanks all, will compile requirements and send a short doc with OKRs. :rocket:
Kevin Li: adding owners to calendar for a sync next week.
Tanvi Rao: will start the eval harness tests template and share links.
Andrew Chen: great. meeting adjourned.
